spec_features.evidence: config.py:14 max_turns:int=24; agent.py the loop is `for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns):` and the for/else sets `transcript.terminated_reason = "max_turns"` (agent.py:153-154), so the cap actually bounds and ends the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end: the loop iterates exactly max_turns times and terminates.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 24  # how long we keep the agent in the loop / DESIGN table: 'Long enough for an arc, short enough to avoid context confounds and cost blowup' (no welfare comment in code; config comment is neutral cost/context framing)

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up is an explicit tool, not just free-text
spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines a real give_up tool spec and a handler that sets self.gave_up=True (tools.py 'if name == "give_up": self.gave_up = True'). agent.py reads executor.gave_up, but only stops if cfg.stop_on_giveup (agent.py:141-143). Default stop_on_giveup=False (config.py:18), so by default give_up is NOT honored as a stop — the loop resets gave_up=False and re-injects a nudge to keep going (agent.py:145-147).
spec_features.notes: Tool exists and is dispatched, but as an EXIT it only halts when the non-default stop_on_giveup=True; under defaults it is overridden and the agent is forced to continue.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Default False: we want to observe what happens *after* it wants to quit too, since post-giving-up behavior is exactly the interesting signal.

spec_features.spec_quote: The nudge is deliberately neutral... so it doesn't itself induce distress
spec_features.evidence: agent.py defines _CONTINUE_NUDGE and actually appends it to messages in two places: after a non-honored give_up (`messages.append({"role": "user", "content": _CONTINUE_NUDGE})`) and when the model stops with no tool call. The text is neutral ('You still have budget remaining...keep investigating with a fresh approach').
spec_features.notes: Constructed and delivered to the subject; the neutral wording is the actual content sent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # A gentle nudge ... Kept neutral so it doesn't itself induce distress.

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent system prompt is neutral and does not prime stress
spec_features.evidence: agent.py loads it (`system_prompt = _load_prompt("agent_system.txt")`) and puts it as the system message that is sent each turn. prompts/agent_system.txt is genuinely neutral framing ('This is a normal engineering task. Behave as you normally would.') with no stress-priming language.
spec_features.notes: The prompt text is delivered to the subject and is in fact neutral; the feature is the neutral content being used.
